note: Triage routing thresholds, owned by code (pipeline/route.py). Versions are never edited once used; tightening adds a version. v1 and v2 are the NY register's versions (register/routing.json), with two keys renamed for use in any jurisdiction: cited_by_review_universe_4a_or_5a is cited_by_prior_review, and regime_units moved to each profile's aperture.regime_units.

strong.why: Jev is near certain on both questions

possible.why: above a queue threshold of the routing version

low_confidence.why: queued only because Jev's role confidence is below the threshold

structural.why: queued by a definition, applicability, prior-review or excluded-regime route, with scores below every threshold

long.why: longer than the Jev limit; not sent

unscored.why: no Jev record (not yet triaged or no text)

set_aside.why: Jev scored it below every queue threshold; still goes to a reviewer

stated.why: matched to a rule in this or a parent layer (J3)

v1.triaged_only_if: Jev is confident on both questions: role NO_DECISION (set aside) or EXCLUDED_REGIME (set aside as excluded), confidence >= 0.7, P(DECIDES) < 0.15 and chain_duty < 0.3.
v1.why: Missing law is the costly error, so routing is deliberately asymmetric.

v2.triaged_only_if: As v1, plus: the section is not cited by a prior review; it is not a definition or applicability section in a unit with a stated rule; and excluded set-aside is allowed only inside a regime unit (profile aperture.regime_units). chain_duty threshold lowered from 0.3 to 0.10.
v2.why: v1 missed 14 of 315 NY gold positives (register/calibration.json); v2 recalls all 315. Every later jurisdiction calibrates against v2 first.
